'''Nicholas Jeffrey Ward''' (born September 2, 1997) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State Spartans]].

==High school career==
Nick began playing basketball at a young age and shot the ball right handed despite being naturally left-handed.<ref name=shot/> He starred at [[Lincoln High School (Gahanna, Ohio)|Lincoln High School]] in [[Gahanna, Ohio]] and averaged 21.0 points and 8.5 rebounds per game as a senior. He verbally committed to Michigan State in April 2015.<ref name=emerges>{{Cite news|last=Quinn|first=Brendan|url=http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2016/10/just_like_that_nick_ward_unexp.html|title=Just like that, Nick Ward unexpectedly emerges as Michigan State's most important freshman|work=MLive.com|access-date=May 29, 2018|date=October 20, 2016}}</ref> Ward was a four-star prospect and a consensus top-50 recruit in the 2016 class.<ref name=shot>{{Cite news|last=Quinn|first=Brendan|url=http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2016/11/nick_ward_1.html|title=At Michigan State, Nick Ward is getting the shot his father never got to take|work=MLive.com|access-date=May 29, 2018|date=December 2, 2016}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On June 21, 2019, Ward signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]] to play for their [[NBA Summer League]] team.

On September 2, 2019, Ward signed his first professional contract with [[Hapoel Gilboa Galil]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Hapoel Gilboa announces Nick Ward|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/hapoel-gilboa-announces-nick-ward/|date=September 2, 2019|access-date=September 2, 2019|work=Sportando}}</ref> On September 25, 2019, he parted ways with Gilboa Galil after appearing in one pre-season tournament game.<ref>{{cite news|title=Gilboa Galil signs Jarvis Varnado|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/gilboa-galil-signs-jarvis-varnado/|date=September 25, 2019|access-date=September 25, 2019|work=Sportando|archive-date=September 25, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190925075625/https://sportando.basketball/en/gilboa-galil-signs-jarvis-varnado/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On September 28, 2019, Ward signed with Fethiye Belediyespor of the [[Turkish Basketball First League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Nick Ward Lokman Hekim Fethiye Belediyespor'da|url=https://gercekfethiye.com/nick-ward-lokman-hekim-fethiye-belediyesporda/20969/|date=September 28, 2019|access-date=October 18, 2019|work=GercekFethiye.com|language=tr}}</ref> In 4 games played for Belediyespor, he averaged 22 points and 6.2 rebounds per game. On November 15, 2019, Ward parted ways with Belediyespor.

On November 15, 2019, Ward signed with the [[College Park Skyhawks]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Nick Ward joins College Park Skyhawks|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/nick-ward-joins-college-park-skyhawks/|date=November 15, 2019|access-date=November 17, 2019|work=Sportando.basketball}}</ref> Ward posted 22 points and 18 rebounds in a loss to the [[Grand Rapids Drive]] on January 15, 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hollins Impressive in Drive Road Win |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/hollins-impressive-in-drive-road-win/n-5589560 |website=OurSportsCentral |accessdate=June 21, 2020 |date=January 15, 2020}}</ref> He averaged 13.2 points and 6.5 rebounds per game for the Skyhawks.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Brooks |first1=Stephen |title=Tom Izzo: Social media rumors about Nick Ward are untrue |url=https://247sports.com/college/michigan-state/Article/Nick-Ward-social-media-rumors-hospital-Tom-Izzo-145462982/ |accessdate=June 21, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=March 27, 2020}}</ref>

On October 25, 2020, Ward signed with [[Istanbul Basket]] of the [[Turkish Basketball First League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Istanbul lands Nick Ward |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/650115/Istanbul-lands-Nick-Ward |website=Eurobasket |accessdate=October 25, 2020 |date=October 25, 2020}}</ref>

On March 26, 2021, Ward signed with the [[Ottawa Blackjacks]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ottawa BlackJacks Sign NBA G-League And Michigan State Alumni Nick Ward|url=https://www.cebl.ca/ottawa-blackjacks-sign-nba-g-league-and-michigan-state-alumni-nick-ward|website=CEBL.ca|accessdate=March 30, 2021|date=March 26, 2021}}</ref> In October, he signed with [[Básquet Coruña]] of the [[Liga Española de Baloncesto|LEB Oro]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Spanish LEB Gold round 2 best performance Nick Ward (by Hoops Agents) |url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/Spain/news/709540/Spanish-LEB-Gold-round-2-best-performance-Nick-Ward-(by-Hoops-Agents) |website=Eurobasket |access-date=December 18, 2021 |date=October 15, 2021}}</ref>

On August 21, 2023, Ward signed with [[KB Prishtina|Sigal Prishtina]] of the [[Kosovo Basketball Superleague]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Prishtina tabs Nick Ward, ex Vancouver |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Kosovo/news/825459/Prishtina-tabs-Nick-Ward-ex-Vancouver|website=Eurobasket.com|date=August 21, 2023|accessdate=28 November 2023}}</ref> On October 13, he signed with [[BC Gargždai-SC|BC Gargždai]] of the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]] (LKL).<ref>{{cite web|title="Gargžduose" J. Juciką keičia amerikietis|url=https://lkl.lt/straipsniai/7032/gargzduose-j-jucika-keicia-amerikietis|website=lkl.lt|language=lt|date=October 13, 2023|accessdate=28 November 2023}}</ref>

On September 2, 2024, Ward signed with [[Sporting CP (basketball)|Sporting CP]] of the [[Liga Portuguesa de Basquetebol]].<ref>{{cite web|author=sportingmodalidades|title=A cara nova do #BasquetebolSCP comemora hoje o seu aniversário 🥳 Parabéns, @nickward44 🎂 #BdaySCP|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/C_1U1e8P7Rn/?img_index=1|website=Instagram.com|date=September 2, 2024|access-date=October 22, 2024|language=Portuguese}}</ref>

Ward joined Big X, a team composed primarily of former Big Ten players in [[The Basketball Tournament 2020]]. He led Big X with 18 points in a 79–74 win over alternate D2 in the first round.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Prescott |first1=Adam |title=Big X Wins TBT Opener, Former Buckeye C.J. Jackson Makes Game-Winning Basket |url=https://www.si.com/college/ohiostate/basketball/big-x-tbt-opener-2020 |accessdate=July 5, 2020 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=July 4, 2020}}</ref>
